key_observations: Stability gate failed (fell_over_rate=1.82 > 0.5) at only 758/3000 iterations; Rule 2 edge case but gait metrics confirm genuine trouble, not just early noise.
Both gait CV targets moved in the wrong direction: gait_air_cv_mean 0.247→0.270, gait_contact_cv_mean 0.334→0.567 (much worse) — the primary hypothesis did not hold.

The 5× increase in angular_momentum_reward_weight (−0.01→−0.05) is the prime destabilisation suspect: it competes with the torso dynamics needed for counterswing and may have conflicted with balance, producing the failed stability gate.
Exploration health is normal (entropy declining gradually, action_std=0.67) — the policy is learning locomotion but the reward landscape is too conflicted for stable periodic gait to emerge.
Symmetry shows the mirror-pose limp pattern (symmetry_pos_cost_mean=0.0027 low but symmetry_vel_cost_mean=0.091 elevated), consistent with the high contact CV irregularity.
Landing force (42 N) and per-step reward trend are both healthy — the failure is specifically in gait rhythm and stability, not in the reward signal quality overall.
next_suggestion: Revert angular_momentum_reward_weight to −0.01 while keeping gait_phase_regularity_reward_weight at −2.5 and shoulder_pitch_std at 0.35. This isolates whether the stronger regularity penalty alone can drive CV metrics down without the destabilising angular momentum interaction. Watch for track_linear_velocity to dip slightly as the expected Rule 6 side effect confirming the regularity weight is actually doing work.
